meta.name: 31 Euphrosyne
meta.note: 31 Euphrosyne (C-type) is a main-belt asteroid; this is its brightness in 155 SPHEREx frames, each frame at a different wavelength, not a reflectance spectrum.
meta.method: The position of the asteroid at each SPHEREx exposure comes from JPL Horizons as seen from the SPHEREx spacecraft, and every exposure whose detector held that position was cut out. The flux is the sum of the calibrated image inside a 3-pixel-radius circle at the centroid, minus the median of a sky ring, times the pixel size, and the wavelength is read at that pixel.
caveats: Fluxes, not reflectance: the Sun's spectrum is not divided out and no thermal model is fitted. Beyond about 3.5 um the asteroid's own heat dominates at this distance from the Sun.
Each frame is a different time and wavelength, so the spin of the asteroid and wavelength are mixed between neighbouring points.
Positions are good to about 1 arcsec (6.15 arcsec pixels), not MPC-grade, and are as seen from SPHEREx at the mid-time of each exposure.

OUTLIER-flagged pixels are kept (moving objects get that flag). Of 220 frames, removed: saturated pixel in the aperture (4), masked pixel (26), another source within 6 px (32), near the detector edge (3), more than 6 arcsec off the prediction (0), no usable sky (0). Points below S/N 5 are kept without a centroid.
No aperture correction and no colour correction; the aperture holds about 98% of a point source.
